class: T4 real-model measurement (256-token short-context, 3 independent server runs; decision-support data for the non-bit-exact split production question)
purpose: quantify the ACTUAL cost of accepting the non-bit-exact split route as the production default, per the owner's 'complete the measurements before judging' direction
setup: request = decode-longout-stability-20260926 (prompt 1089 tokens, max_tokens 256, temperature 0.0, seed 42); decode runs at S~1089-1344 so the split path (S>=512) is active for the whole decode; 3 independent server starts (baseline / split-r1 / split-r2), each confirmed idle (0 procs, 48GB avail) before the next, each with its own ready line + witness
validity: the first attempt was INVALID (split servers failed to start on OOM, all 3 responses hit the single baseline server -> 0/256 was baseline vs itself); discarded and re-run with start-failure detection + idle gating. This record is the valid re-run.
oracle_gate_finding: the pinned BF16 oracle gate is max_model_len=128 (reference_oracle.cpp rejects !=128), so it NEVER exercises the split path (S>=512). 'Does split pass the oracle gate' is therefore a non-question for the long path; the long path is already 'evaluation-route-not-release-qualified' by contract (server ready line). The oracle gate is not a blocker; release-qualification status is a separate contract question.

rate_ms_per_step.note: the split gain is concentrated at long context (1.214x at S~40000); at short context it is negligible (1.013x) because the 6x GQA redundancy volume is small and L2-resident there

nondeterminism_quantified.interpretation: two independent split runs agree for the first 118 tokens then drift; the divergence is not from token 1 at this context length (it was at token 1 for P40000/O16)

baseline_degeneration_observation.fact: the bit-exact baseline run degenerated into a repeat loop at token 55 ('vllmEvn\n' x3, then 'README.md' repeats) while the split runs stayed coherent ('work is explicitly out of scope.')
baseline_degeneration_observation.status: single-sample observation, not a conclusion; recorded as data. It shows bit-exact is NOT a quality guarantee -- a deterministic path can be deterministically wrong. It does NOT make non-determinism free; it only weakens the 'bit-exact = safer' assumption.
baseline_degeneration_observation.no_conclusion: per the verify-first direction this is logged as a measurement, not used to claim split is 'better'

cost_summary_for_owner_decision.gain: 1.214x decode at long context (P40000 159 vs 193 ms/step); ~1.013x at short context (negligible)
cost_summary_for_owner_decision.cost_1_determinism: output is non-deterministic; two runs agree ~118 tokens then drift; seed=42+temperature=0 no longer guarantees byte-reproducible output
cost_summary_for_owner_decision.cost_2_verification: loses the byte-identity regression check that has guarded every decode optimization so far
cost_summary_for_owner_decision.cost_3_release_status: the long path is 'evaluation-route-not-release-qualified'; making it default changes the release-qualification contract
cost_summary_for_owner_decision.not_a_cost: quality does not visibly collapse (both outputs coherent; baseline itself degenerated in this sample)
